summary: 1928 steel fire tower on Oak Hill near Concord, NH, raised 10 feet in 1971 and returned to service in 1991; standing, reached by trail through Oak Hill City Forest.

facts.design: 55-foot steel tower built 1928 with a visitor observation platform just below the cab; raised 10 feet in 1971

staffing.status: part of the state network after 1991; no current staffing source found

access.note: Reached on foot by a trail from the Oak Hill City Forest lot on Shaker Road. No official rule on climbing the tower was found.

visit.trail_note: Park at the Oak Hill City Forest lot on Shaker Road and follow the trail to the summit. A 2025 hiking blog describes the climb as steep and narrow. Ask the land manager before climbing.

facts.agency: NH Dept. of Resources and Economic Development

events.note: Steel tower constructed at 55 feet with a visitor observation platform below the cab

Governor and council began eminent domain proceedings for about two acres on the hill after the owners refused to sell to the state; the state wanted rights of way for power and telephone lines and access to a spring
Returned to full service, first with a volunteer lookout and then as part of the state network
Tower cab replaced and other work done

corrections.why: The 2019 chapter report says the tower cab was replaced and other work was done. It does not say the tower was restored to service.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The sources do not agree on the town: a 1929 notice says Loudon, near the Concord line; a 1947 item says Concord; the Register gives Merrimack County and says not far from Concord; a 2025 blog says the trail crosses the Concord and Loudon line. The story names Merrimack County and does not pick one town.

sources.title: Oak Hill Fire Tower via Sharker Road (Oak Hill City Forest)

notes_for_editor: Most history comes from the Register and a 1929/1947 newspaper excerpt quoted on the Forest Lookouts page; the 1947 article is not checked against the original paper. The 2019 chapter report does not name the tower's operator and its staffing line is for the state's towers in general, not Oak Hill, so staffing is left as historical only. Its staffing line also rests on one member's account, as the report says. The 19.8 m height is from OpenStreetMap, not from the Register. The blog spells the road Sharker in its URL and Shaker in its text; the story uses Shaker. Climbing is described in one hiking blog only; no official rule was found, so the story does not say the tower is open to climb. Lead for later: any Concord or Loudon city or town record that confirms the tower's ownership and public access.
